comparator.name: Law
comparator.sourceNotes: The 180 EC degree comprises 67.5 EC of common law courses and graduation work, 67.5 EC of law courses in the selected route, and 45 EC of non-law electives.
components: Introduction to the Law of Obligations
Introduction to Constitutional and Administrative Law
Graduation Project in International and European Law
Choose one of four graduation projects. Start after earning 120 EC, including all first-year courses.
Private Law in Perspective: Employment Law
This example takes Employment Law within Private Law in Perspective.
Choose 45 EC outside law. With these law choices, take at least 7.5 EC at advanced level and at least 15 EC at intermediate level or above in total.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Legal foundations, interpretation, argument, justice and independent legal research
Constitutional, administrative and criminal law governing public authority and accountability
Private law, obligations, property and civil disputes
European Union and public international law
Law in societal context and legal responses to change
adjacent: Notarial, professional and applied private-law practice
Legal philosophy, fairness and professional judgment
Technology, social change and emerging legal questions
questions: How do legal rules determine rights, obligations and the resolution of disputes?
How should law balance legality, justice and protection of vulnerable people?
How can legal institutions constrain public power and respond to social change?

candidates.label: Notarial Law
candidates.assessment: UCR private and commercial law supports related interests. The workbook does not establish a notarial sequence in family law, registration, property and taxation or Dutch notarial practice.

routeSelection.basis: The multidisciplinary route pairs a general legal curriculum with study outside law. The example takes the first eight listed route choices and the first listed option within Private Law in Perspective. The graduation project is the first of the four listed options.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the generic legal-foundations, rights, justice and social-change interests. Two generator-backed directions are feasible and materially distinct: public, international and European law, and private law, business and commercial relations. The three alternatives differ substantially in course composition and organising emphasis, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

alternatives.label: Law, Politics and Society
alternatives.labelReason: The completed UCR curriculum combines its full available law sequence with politics, sociology, economics, philosophy, research and communication. The label states that interdisciplinary composition and does not imply a Dutch qualifying law degree.
alternatives.concept: Study how law structures society. Explore private, criminal, constitutional, European and international law alongside rights, politics, economics and social research.
progression: Law, Society & Justice in semester 1 precedes every advanced law course that formally requires it. Research Methods & Statistics precedes the selected economics courses with that prerequisite. Introductory politics, sociology, economics and ethics precede advanced EU politics, social theory, public economics, conflict study and research. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Public, International and European Law
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum concentrates constitutional and international law, EU law and politics, comparative institutions, conflict, history and social movements without implying a complete Dutch-law curriculum.
alternatives.concept: Study how public power is organized and held accountable. Connect constitutional, European and international law with comparative politics, conflict, public economics and historical research.
alternatives.distinctness: This plan differs from the broad plan by 6 courses in each direction and from the other focused plan by 12 courses.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes constitutional, international and EU law. Comparative politics, international-relations theory, sociology, economics and research methods precede advanced EU politics, conflict, social theory, international governance and historical research. Business Foundations precedes International Business & Governance. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Law, Business and Technology
alternatives.labelReason: The plan links private and cross-border commercial law to finance, regulation, technological change and market research.
alternatives.concept: Study how law shapes business across borders and how technology changes commercial decisions. Explore private law, trade, contracts and regulation alongside accounting, finance, negotiation and market research.
alternatives.distinctness: This plan differs from the broad plan by 11 courses in each direction and from the other focused plan by 12 courses.
progression: Law, Society & Justice and Business Foundations establish the legal and commercial strands before advanced private, EU, transnational-business and international-governance courses. Research Methods & Statistics precedes negotiation, public economics, econometrics and market research. The final year concentrates private law, international business, social theory, advanced communication, finance, econometrics and applied research. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

blocks: Utrecht introduces the foundations of Dutch law. UCR offers related comparative study of legal systems.
Both examine law through legal, social and normative perspectives.
Utrecht studies general jurisprudence. UCR’s ethics and political philosophy courses support normative reasoning about law.
Both examine treaties, international legal institutions and state responsibility.
Both examine public institutions and the limits of public power. UCR uses a comparative approach.
Both examine the EU legal order, institutions and the relationship between EU and domestic law.
Utrecht offers a separate course in Dutch administrative law.
Utrecht develops Dutch constitutional law beyond its introductory course.
Utrecht develops European law beyond its introductory course.
Both examine obligations and contractual relationships. UCR places these in a broader comparative private-law course.
Both introduce criminal responsibility and legal reasoning. UCR approaches criminal law comparatively.
Utrecht offers a separate introduction to property law. UCR covers related topics within private law.
Utrecht develops Dutch property law in a separate later course.
Utrecht builds on its introduction with a separate substantive criminal-law course.
Utrecht builds on its introduction with a separate obligations course.
Utrecht studies litigation and administrative proceedings in the Dutch system.
Utrecht focuses on employment law. UCR offers cross-border business law.
Utrecht requires an independent legal project. UCR shows optional independent research separately.
Choose non-law electives, including at least 7.5 EC at advanced level and at least 15 EC at intermediate level or above in total.

notes.text: Utrecht offers a continuous sequence in Dutch law, procedure and legal research. The UCR plans combine comparative legal study with social science and business. Eligibility for regulated Dutch legal professions depends on further legal study and the applicable professional requirements.

Utrecht’s regulations describe exemptions that eligible UCR graduates can request. The listed exemptions depend on the courses completed and the Utrecht route chosen. Check the current regulations before planning a transfer.

audience.programmeDescription: This Dutch-taught law degree covers legal reasoning and the Dutch, European and international legal systems.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Utrecht example combines law with non-law electives. The UCR plans explore law and society, public and cross-border law, or law and business.
